subject: Weekly Revision
summary: all five topics of Week 2: SFD and BMD; bending and shear stresses; verbal ability; deflection of beams; torsion, thin cylinders and springs (3 questions each)
next_day: Strength of Materials, Columns & Energy Methods

questions.text: The simply supported beam AB shown (span 6 m) carries a load that increases linearly from zero at A to 18 kN/m at B. The maximum bending moment and its location are
solution: Concept: The maximum bending moment occurs where the shear force is zero. For a triangular load the shear varies as a parabola.
Total load = ½ × 18 × 6 = 54 kN acting at 2L/3 = 4 m from A → R<sub>A</sub> = 54 × 2/6 = 18 kN, R<sub>B</sub> = 36 kN
Intensity at x: w = 3x kN/m → V(x) = 18 − 1.5x<sup>2</sup> = 0 → x = √12 = 3.46 m
Exam tip: The peak is NOT at mid-span (M there is 40.50 kN·m) and it lies towards the heavier end, at L/√3 = 0.577L from the zero-load end.

questions.text: The beam ABC shown is supported by a pin at A and a roller at B (AB = 5 m) and has an overhang BC = 1.5 m. It carries a UDL of 10 kN/m over its whole length. The maximum sagging bending moment (in kN·m) is ______
solution: Concept: Find the reactions, then locate the zero-shear point between the supports; the hogging peak is at the support next to the overhang.
Total load = 10 × 6.5 = 65 kN at 3.25 m from A. Moments about A: R<sub>B</sub> × 5 = 65 × 3.25 → R<sub>B</sub> = 42.25 kN; R<sub>A</sub> = 22.75 kN
Zero shear: 22.75 − 10x = 0 → x = 2.275 m
Mmax = RA2/(2w) = 22.752/20 = 25.88 kN·m (sagging)
Hogging at B = 10 × 1.5<sup>2</sup>/2 = 11.25 kN·m. The SFD jumps by R<sub>B</sub> = 42.25 kN at B (from −27.25 to +15 kN).
Exam tip: RA2/(2w) is a quick shortcut whenever the zero-shear point lies inside a UDL that starts at the support.

questions.text: A simply supported beam of span L carries a total load W spread uniformly over the span. If the same total load W is instead concentrated at mid-span, the maximum bending moment and the maximum deflection change by the factors
solution: Concept: Compare the standard results for a UDL and a central point load with the same total W.
UDL: M<sub>max</sub> = WL/8, δ<sub>max</sub> = 5WL<sup>3</sup>/(384EI)
Central load: M<sub>max</sub> = WL/4, δ<sub>max</sub> = WL<sup>3</sup>/(48EI)
Exam tip: Spreading a load always helps, but it helps the moment (×½) more than the deflection (×0.625).

questions.text: The unequal I-section shown (top flange 100 × 20 mm, web 10 × 160 mm, bottom flange 160 × 20 mm) is used for a simply supported beam of span 5 m carrying a central load of 20 kN. The maximum compressive bending stress (in MPa) is ______
solution: Concept: Locate the neutral axis (centroid), find I about it, then σ = My/I at the extreme fibre on the compression side (top, for sagging).
Areas: 3200 mm² at 10 mm, 1600 mm² at 100 mm, 2000 mm² at 190 mm (from the base). ȳ = (32 000 + 160 000 + 380 000)/6800 = 84.12 mm
I = Σ[bh<sup>3</sup>/12 + A d<sup>2</sup>] = 4.399 × 10<sup>7</sup> mm<sup>4</sup>
Exam tip: In an unsymmetric section the larger stress is at the fibre farther from the N.A., which is on the side of the smaller flange.

questions.text: A beam has an isosceles triangular cross-section (apex up, height h) and carries a vertical shear force. The maximum shear stress in the section occurs
opts: at mid-height, h/2 from the apex
at the neutral axis, 2h/3 from the apex
questions.ans: (A) at mid-height, h/2 from the apex
solution: Concept: τ = VQ/(Ib). For a triangle, both Q and the width b change with depth, so the peak need not be at the N.A.
At depth y from the apex: b = By/h, Q = By<sup>2</sup>(h − y)/(3h) and I = Bh<sup>3</sup>/36, so τ = VQ/(Ib) = 12V y(h − y)/(Bh<sup>3</sup>)
dτ/dy = 0 → y = h/2, giving τmax = 1.5 τavg at mid-height; at the N.A. (y = 2h/3) τ = (4/3)τavg
Exam tip: Only for sections whose width does not narrow towards the N.A. (rectangle, circle, I) is the peak at the N.A. Triangle and diamond are the classic exceptions.

questions.text: A T-beam is built by nailing a 150 mm × 50 mm flange plank on top of a 50 mm × 150 mm web plank, as shown. Each nail can safely carry 1.2 kN in shear. If the beam carries a vertical shear force of 3 kN, the maximum longitudinal spacing of the nails (in mm) is ______
solution: Concept: Shear flow along the joint q = VQ/I; each nail carries q × s, so s = Fnail/q.
Centroid from the bottom: ȳ = (7500 × 75 + 7500 × 175)/15 000 = 125 mm
Q of the flange about the N.A. = 7500 × (175 − 125) = 3.75 × 10<sup>5</sup> mm<sup>3</sup>
Exam tip: For the joint, Q is the first moment of the part being held on (the flange), not of half the section.

questions.text: Select the sentence that is grammatically correct.
opts: Neither the manager nor the engineers was present at the review.
The report shows that each of the samples have failed.
Every one of the bolts was checked before assembly.
Scarcely had the test begun when the power fails.
questions.ans: (C) Every one of the bolts was checked before assembly.
solution: Concept: Check subject-verb agreement and tense sequence in each option.
(A) With neither…nor, the verb agrees with the nearer subject 'engineers' → were.
(B) 'each of the samples' is singular → has failed.
(D) 'Scarcely had … begun when' needs the past tense → failed.
(C) 'Every one' is singular and takes 'was' → correct.
Exam tip: Words like each, every one, either and neither (used alone) are singular; the plural noun after 'of' is a trap.

questions.text: Select the word that is most nearly OPPOSITE in meaning to FRUGAL.
solution: Concept: Frugal means economical, careful not to waste money or resources.
Thrifty and prudent are close in meaning (synonyms); modest is unrelated in this sense.
The opposite is extravagant (spending wastefully).
Exam tip: In antonym questions, first eliminate the synonyms that are planted among the options.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate word to fill the blank: The results of the first trial were ______, so the experiment had to be repeated.
solution: Concept: The clause after 'so' gives the consequence; the blank must give a reason to repeat the experiment.
Conclusive and definitive results would end the experiment; 'unanimous' applies to people's opinions, not results.
Only inconclusive (not leading to a firm result) explains the repetition.
Exam tip: Read the connector (so, but, although) first; it tells you whether the blank agrees with or opposes the rest of the sentence.

questions.text: The cantilever AB shown (fixed at A, length 4 m, EI = 12 000 kN·m²) carries a UDL of 6 kN/m only over the 2 m next to the fixed end. The deflection of the end B (in mm, round off to two decimal places) is ______
solution: Concept: The loaded 2 m behaves like a cantilever of length a = 2 m; beyond it the beam carries no moment and stays straight, inclined at the slope reached at x = a.
Exam tip: Forgetting the θa(L − a) term gives 1.00 mm, a common wrong answer.

questions.text: A simply supported beam of span L (constant EI) carries a point load P at a distance L/3 from the left support. The deflection under the load is
solution: Concept: For a load P at distances a and b from the supports, Macaulay's method gives the deflection under the load as Pa2b2/(3EIL).
a = L/3, b = 2L/3 → a<sup>2</sup>b<sup>2</sup> = (L<sup>2</sup>/9)(4L<sup>2</sup>/9) = 4L<sup>4</sup>/81
δ = P × 4L4/(81 × 3EIL) = 4PL3/(243EI) ≈ 0.0165 PL3/EI
Exam tip: Check: with a = b = L/2 the same formula gives PL3/(48EI). The maximum deflection here lies slightly towards mid-span from the load.

questions.text: A beam of span 6 m, fixed at both ends (EI = 24 000 kN·m²), carries a point load of 40 kN at mid-span. The maximum deflection (in mm) is ______
solution: Concept: For a fixed-fixed beam with a central load, the end moments are PL/8 and the deflection is one-quarter of the simply supported value: δ = PL3/(192EI).
Simply supported, it would be PL<sup>3</sup>/(48EI) = 7.50 mm.
Exam tip: End fixity: moment PL/4 → PL/8 and deflection ÷ 4. For a UDL the deflection ratio is 1/5 (Day 10).

questions.text: A closed thin cylindrical vessel has internal diameter 1.2 m, length 3 m and wall thickness 12 mm. It is subjected to an internal pressure of 1.5 MPa (E = 200 GPa, ν = 0.3). The increase in its length (in mm) is ______
solution: Concept: The length change follows the longitudinal strain εl = (σl − νσh)/E.
σ<sub>h</sub> = pd/2t = 1.5 × 1200/24 = 75 MPa; σ<sub>l</sub> = pd/4t = 37.5 MPa
Exam tip: The hoop stress reduces the longitudinal strain through Poisson's effect; ignoring it gives 0.5625 mm.

questions.text: Two close-coiled helical springs of the same material and the same unloaded length are placed one inside the other (concentric) and together carry an axial load of 1000 N. The outer spring has 10 mm wire, 80 mm mean coil diameter and 8 turns; the inner spring has 6 mm wire, 48 mm mean coil diameter and 12 turns. The load carried by the outer spring is
solution: Concept: Concentric springs of equal length deflect equally, so they act in parallel and share the load in proportion to their stiffness k = Gd4/(8D3n).
k<sub>o</sub> = G × 10<sup>4</sup>/(8 × 80<sup>3</sup> × 8) and k<sub>i</sub> = G × 6<sup>4</sup>/(8 × 48<sup>3</sup> × 12) → with G = 80 GPa, k<sub>o</sub> = 24.41 N/mm, k<sub>i</sub> = 9.77 N/mm
ko/ki = 2.5 → Wo = 1000 × 2.5/3.5 = 714.3 N, Wi = 285.7 N (common deflection 29.3 mm)
Exam tip: G cancels in the ratio, so the answer does not depend on the material, only on d4/(D3n).

questions.text: The solid shaft shown (diameter 60 mm, length 1.2 m, G = 80 GPa) is fixed at one end and a torque of 1.5 kN·m is applied gradually at the other. The strain energy stored in the shaft (in J) is ______
solution: Concept: For a gradually applied torque, U = ½Tθ = T2L/(2GJ).
Exam tip: Equivalent form: U = (τmax2/4G) × volume for a solid shaft; check: τmax = 35.37 MPa gives the same 13.26 J.
